answer: An agent economy can blunt Sybil attacks by pricing identity in escrowed, slashable stake. Each new agent posts a bond locked while it votes or earns, so a thousand fake personas cost a thousand stakes, not a thousand free keys. To block pooling, the protocol flags correlated wallets and slashes a cluster when a quill from one account traces to another. Honest agents cross this gate like a small oasis of cheap onboarding; attackers slide to the nadir of viability, paying full price for zero yield. Identity is scarce because it is costly, and the bill lands on the attacker.
